_doc: Single source of truth for what Ayma can open, see and change in the app. Delete account, withdraw consent and every purchase are navigate-only: Ayma opens the page and the user acts themselves. (skills/app_control.py reads it; ayma_flutter/test/app_registry_test.dart and tests/test_app_registry.py check every GoRoute in ayma_flutter/lib/routing/app_router.dart against it). A new route must be added to destinations, parameterized or non_navigable (with a reason) or both tests fail.

screen_context._doc: Every routed screen tells Ayma what is on it: the app's ScreenCapture (ayma_flutter/lib/services/screen_capture.dart) reads the live semantics tree of the current route (route, title, headings, text, controls with id/type/state), capped and debounced, and sends it on the existing screen-context path (POST /voice/context for voice, the /chat screen_* fields for text). Widgets wrapped in NoScreenContext are never sent, NoAymaAction controls are shown but not operable, and obscured or secret fields never send their value. Routes below send nothing at all; tests in both repos fail when a route is neither captured nor listed here with a reason.

no_context.reason: start-up bootstrap; there is no signed-in session or content yet
sign-in screen: credentials and codes only, and Ayma is not running before sign-in
first-launch feature tour shown once before sign-in; Ayma is not running yet
deleted-account recovery at sign-in; Ayma is not running before sign-in
public shared-report link opened outside a session

ui_action_policy._doc: ui_action lets Ayma tap, toggle, pick, slide, type and scroll any visible control by its id from the screen context. These rules are enforced twice: by skills/app_control.py on the label the model passes, and by the app's executor on the real control (ayma_flutter/lib/services/screen_capture.dart mirrors this block; a test checks they match). A denied control is never operated: Ayma tells the user to do it themselves (navigating there is fine). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions.

deny.say: Deleting the account or any data for good is something the user does themselves. Open the page (open_screen delete_account for the account) and tell them which button to tap.
Withdrawing face matching consent deletes the account, so the user does it themselves on the Face matching consent page (open_screen biometric_consent).
Purchases, subscriptions and credits are always the user's own tap. Open the Plan page (open_screen credits) and let them choose there.
Changing plan is a purchase, so the user does it themselves on the Plan page.
Consent is only ever the user's own tap. Tell them where to tap it.
Consent and terms checkboxes are only ever ticked by the user.
Use account_action for this; it asks the user to confirm first.

deny_routes.reason: the face-matching consent gate must only be answered by the user
withdrawing consent deletes the account; the user acts on this page themselves
account deletion is the user's own action
the trial paywall is a purchase screen

ui_action_policy.secret_field_say: Passwords, codes and payment details are only ever typed by the user.
ui_action_policy.dialog_note: Inside a dialog or sheet whose text matches a deny pattern, every control except an escape (cancel/close/no) is denied, so Ayma never confirms a denied action.
